name: Casona de Sánchez de Tagle
summary: Late-17th-century mansion in the old town of Santillana, listed among the buildings of interest on the official town map and in the municipal guide. Seen from the street.

name: Ermita de San Roque (Santillana del Mar)
summary: Small chapel marked as a building of interest on the official Santillana town map. The town's San Roque festivity falls on 16 August.
uncertain: Only named on the map legend; no description in the guide.

guide: Santillana Del Mar, un lugar para admirar
name: Antigua Cárcel (Santillana del Mar)
summary: The old jail of Santillana, marked on the 'un lugar para admirar' monuments map as an exhibition space in the historic centre, near the town hall.
uncertain: Map label only; opening times and current use not stated.

guide: Santillana Del Mar, un lugar para admirar
name: Salón del Tiempo (Santillana del Mar)
summary: An exhibition space shown on the official illustrated monuments map of Santillana, in the lower part of the town near the Barreda-Bracho house (Parador).
uncertain: Map label only; no description, hours or prices.

guide: Santillana Del Mar, un lugar para admirar
name: Casa de Doña Paz de Borbón
summary: Historic house in central Santillana, marked as a building of interest on the official illustrated monuments map, close to the Torre del Merino and the Plaza Mayor.
uncertain: Map label only; no description in the guide.

guide: Santillana Del Mar, un lugar para admirar
name: Casa de los Bustamante (Santillana del Mar)
summary: Noble house in Santillana marked on the illustrated monuments map and given its own entry in the municipal tourist guide's civil-heritage chapter; one of the family houses whose arms appear around the town.
uncertain: Guide section text was largely unreadable (font encoding); only the name and map position label confirmed.

name: Aparcamiento Plaza del Rey (Santillana del Mar)
summary: One of the two public car parks for visitors to Santillana: cars are restricted to residents inside the old town, so visitors leave the car here. Reached from the CA-133.
facts: Old town traffic restricted to residents; cobbled streets, wear comfortable shoes

name: Aparcamiento de Rolaceña (Santillana del Mar)
summary: Public car park next to the tourist office, the second official parking area for visitors to the car-free historic centre of Santillana. Reached from the CA-131.
facts: From the CA-131, beside the tourist office

name: Torre de Don Beltrán de la Cueva
summary: Battlemented three-storey stone tower from the late 15th or early 16th century, with a 17th-century mansion attached, a few metres from Queveda's parish church. Listed as a heritage site in 1981. A 5 km circular walk from Queveda via Mijares passes it.

name: Ermita de la Virgen de las Nieves (de las Quintas)
summary: 18th-century chapel in Queveda with rubble walls and dressed-stone corners, keeping a Solomonic-style altarpiece with its original images. Its festivity, Nuestra Señora de las Quintas, is on 5 August.

name: Ermita de San Sebastián y lavadero (Herrán)
summary: Small late-Gothic chapel (14th century) in Herrán, the village that also holds the zoo and Altamira. A Roman-inscribed tombstone was found here. Nearby are a restored old washing place and a small, very old bridge. A 5.5 km walk from Santillana via the Altamira meadows ends here.
facts: 14th century, over an earlier 9th-10th century chapel

name: Ermita de San Cipriano y San Cornelio (Camplengo)
summary: Small 17th-century chapel in Camplengo, built over a 10th-century church. The village lies on the coastal Way of St James just before Santillana.

name: Palacio de Peredo (Mijares)
summary: Sober 16th-century dressed-stone palace in Mijares, also called the Mijares Palace, with a large Peredo coat of arms and a round-arched doorway carved with plant motifs. Nearby is the 17th-century parish church of San Andrés y Santa María.

name: Castillo de Vispieres (Pico Vispieres / Monte Castillo)
summary: Hilltop south-east of Santillana with ruins of a 15th-century fortress (an almost square rubble building) and possibly an older Cantabrian hill fort. A 2.5 km climb from Santillana towards Torrelavega reaches the summit, a natural viewpoint over the whole municipality.
uncertain: Not the same as the 'Monte Castillo' hike already in Notion (that one is in Central Cantabria / Puente Viesgo).

name: Ermita de San Jorge (Vispieres)
summary: 17th-century chapel in Vispieres with a rectangular nave, square apse and geometric decoration on its round entrance arch. The village also has 17th-century houses with coats of arms (Pérez Bustamante, Bustamante, La Malata).

name: Casa-Torre de los Calderón de la Barca (Viveda)
summary: Medieval tower-house dated to the 13th-15th centuries, among the oldest civil buildings in Cantabria, with battlements and legends of underground passages and a stay by St Francis of Assisi on his pilgrimage. A 5.2 km circular walk from Viveda passes it.
facts: Historic-Artistic Monument 1982; Bien de Interés Local 2002

name: Palacio de Peredo (Viveda)
summary: 17th-century mountain-style mansion in Viveda with a dressed-stone facade and the Peredo y Velarde arms, nicknamed locally the 'palace of the golden pig'. Start and end of a circular walk via the Calderón tower and the Suances-Los Corrales path.

name: Iglesia de San Salvador (Viveda)
summary: Parish church of Viveda, rebuilt in the 16th century over a 10th-century building, keeping a Romanesque doorway with carved capitals and a Gothic arch. Its feast (San Salvador) is on 6 August.

name: Ermita de la Virgen de la Consolación (Yuso)
summary: 17th-century chapel in Yuso, a small village 2 km north-west of Santillana noted in the guide for its wide views over the municipality and its traditional Cantabrian houses.

name: Arroyo: Capilla de Nuestra Señora y Cueva de Arroyo
summary: The smallest village of the municipality, 2 km north-west of Santillana, with 17th-18th-century vernacular houses, a 17th-century chapel and a cave with prehistoric occupation. The long circular walk from Santillana stops at its old fountain and washing place.
uncertain: Cave access is not described; probably not visitable.

name: Torre de San Telmo (Ubiarco)
summary: A lone 14th-century wall, all that remains of a watchtower that guarded this coast, standing on the cliffs near Santa Justa beach and chapel. Reachable on the cliff path from the beach.

name: Calas de La Jerrona y Onzaperas
summary: Two wild coves on the Ubiarco cliffs with numerous 'bufones', narrow channels where waves force out jets of air and spray. Cormorants and gulls are the usual seabirds. La Jerrona is passed on the long walk from Santillana to Santa Justa.

name: Ensenada / Puerto de Calderón
summary: A sheltered inlet among steep cliffs, used as a port since Roman times. A green path with oaks and yews runs from here to Santa Justa beach; it is the highlight of the 10.5/14.5 km circular walk from Santillana.
uncertain: Notion already has the hike 'Acantilados de Santa Justa – Puerto Calderón'; this is the point itself.

name: Parque de La Alianza
summary: A 32,000 m2 park shared by Santillana and Suances municipalities, reached from Barrio Peredo on the Way of St James, with a children's play area, barbecues and rustic picnic furniture.

name: Santillana circular: Rubaña, Arroyo, Calderón and Santa Justa
summary: The longest of four routes suggested by Santillana's tourism website: circular from the town over Rubaña hill to Arroyo, then to the coast past the Calderón inlet, La Jerrona cove and Tresvalle to Ubiarco, returning by the CA-351 and an old cart track past El Cuco and the El Silo barns.
facts: 10.5 km, or 14.5 km including Santa Justa chapel

name: Camino de Santiago: Viveda to Santillana and Arroyo
summary: 9.7 km section of the Way of St James, also fine by bike, from the Puente de la Barca in Viveda past La Alianza park and Camplengo to Santillana, then on towards Arroyo with a view of Oreña. Waymarked with shells and yellow arrows.

name: Santillana to Altamira and Herrán loop
summary: 5.5 km walk from the Revolgo park up through meadows to near the Altamira caves, returning through a eucalyptus wood to the San Sebastián chapel in Herrán and back.

name: Queveda and Mijares loop
summary: 5 km circular walk from Queveda up a eucalyptus hill with views of the village, down to Mijares for the palace and church, and back past the Torre de Don Beltrán de la Cueva.

name: Viveda loop: Calderón tower and old railway
summary: Circular walk of about 5.2 km starting and ending at the Peredo palace in Viveda, via the Calderón de la Barca tower and Riaño along the old railway, returning on the Suances-Los Corrales foot and cycle path under plane trees.
facts: About 5.2 km (300 m shorter than the 5.5 km route)
uncertain: English text says 'only 300 mts'; Spanish says 300 m shorter than the previous 5.5 km route.

name: Casa de Ocejo
summary: Indiano-style house bought in 1865 by the first Marquis of Comillas for his mother. King Alfonso XII stayed here in 1881 and 1882; on 5 September 1881 he chaired a cabinet meeting, making Comillas capital of Spain for a day. Gaudí designed a (lost) Chinese kiosk for its garden. Private property.

name: Casa de La Portilla
summary: Neoclassical summer house of Claudio López, brother of the first marquis, designed in 1871 by Josep Oriol Mestres, with an exterior stair, columned porch and a south gallery painted with Japanese-influenced decoration. The infantas stayed here during the royal visits of 1881-82. Private property.

name: Casa de las Cavaducas
summary: Summer residence built in 1875 for Isabel López Bru, designed by her husband Eusebi Güell, Gaudí's patron. Burnt in 1987 and since rebuilt. Private property within the Sobrellano garden-city ensemble.

name: Casa del Llano
summary: Rectangular prism-shaped summer house of Patricio de Satrústegui, the first marquis's business partner, similar to the Ocejo and La Portilla houses. Private property on the edge of the Sobrellano estate.

name: Mirador y Ermita de Santa Lucía
summary: Simple chapel on a headland above Comillas beach, where fishermen prayed before going to sea. Two small lighthouses stand where whale-spotting lookouts once warned the harpooners. A fine viewpoint over the coast.

name: Corro San Pedro
summary: Traditional square of Comillas framed by noble houses, including an 18th-century mansion with a large coat of arms and the former Parador (later Hotel San Pedro), where the saint's image is kept. On 29 June it is carried in procession with dancers and tambourines.

name: Monumento al Sagrado Corazón de Jesús (Comillas)
summary: Statue of the Sacred Heart on a hill above the town, commissioned by the second marquis; destroyed in the Civil War and rebuilt in the 1940s. Behind it is the Casa Rectoral (about 1770) with its pulpit-like balcony.

name: La Cárcel – Albergue de Peregrinos La Peña
summary: Austere building of 1879 in the La Peña quarter, paid for by neighbours as the town jail with two cells and a courtyard; now a hostel for pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago and the Santo Toribio route.

name: Ayuntamiento Antiguo (Comillas)
summary: Former town hall built on the site of the old hospital and San Juan chapel, with sandstone arcades open to the street on three sides, the shields of the archbishops born in Comillas, and a small market bell on the roof.
uncertain: Built 1780 per the town map; the Comillas guide says 1775.

name: Corro Campíos
summary: The lively main square of Comillas beside the parish church, historically used for bowls, dances and fiestas and still the meeting point of the town, with cafés and restaurants. It opens into the traditional Campíos quarter.

name: Ayuntamiento Nuevo y Plaza del Ángel (Comillas)
summary: Late-19th-century building paid for by Manuela del Piélago as a free infant school run by the Daughters of Charity; since 2003 the town hall. The Plaza del Ángel lies on its south side and a Virgin and Child possibly by Josep Llimona decorates one corner.

name: Fuente de los Tres Caños
summary: Monumental stone fountain and lamp post by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (1899) in the centre of Comillas, honouring Joaquín del Piélago who funded the town's water supply. Shaped like a baroque candelabrum; its light recalls Comillas being the first Spanish town with electric light.

name: Puerta de los Pájaros (Portada Casa Moro)
summary: Gateway of 1900 attributed to Gaudí, built of irregular stone with rounded corners, with three openings: one for carriages, one for people and a small round one for birds, hence its name.

name: La Coteruca
summary: Castle-like summer house on a hill above the sea, built to French plans for the Riera family and later the Marquis of Movellán; a gala ball for the royal family was held here in 1882. Rebuilt as apartments in 1990.

name: Asilo-Hospital de Comillas
summary: Modernist hospital-asylum of 1888 by Cristóbal Cascante, modelled on Sobrellano palace around a central courtyard, with a stepped porch, chapel and wooden mountain-style gallery. Still in use, run by the Daughters of St Joseph.

name: Playa de los Muertos (Comillas)
summary: A tiny bay just beyond the Comillas cemetery, outside the town centre, named in the official guide as Comillas's second beach after the main town beach.
uncertain: Name read from a faint scanned page; location only described as 'beyond the cemetery'.

name: Ría de la Rabia
summary: Tidal estuary west of Comillas, part of the Oyambre Natural Park marshes, with alder, hazel and willow groves and an exceptional bird-watching area where many species feed and winter.

name: Club de Golf Rovacías
summary: Golf course in Comillas, set into the landscape and adapted to the terrain, recommended in the official guide.

name: Arboretum del Joyuco (Rubárcena)
summary: Arboretum between Trasvía and Comillas, near the cycle lane, on the flat land in the bend of the Bárcena river: a rest area planted with a variety of native tree species.

name: Ermita de San Miguel (Rioturbio)
summary: Chapel in Rioturbio, a hamlet inside the Oyambre Natural Park at the edge of the Monte Corona forest, reached along the road across the marshes; the village keeps traditional houses.

name: Ermita de San Andrés (Trasvía)
summary: Chapel in Trasvía, a hamlet on a hill west of Comillas with panoramic views over the Rabia estuary and the Oyambre dunes.

name: Iglesia de San Adrián (Sopeña, Ruiseñada)
summary: Church in the Sopeña quarter of Ruiseñada with 15th-century Gothic details and a columned portico, in a village of rural houses at the foot of Monte Corona.

name: Ermita de Santa Apolonia (La Molina)
summary: Council chapel on the square of Barrio de la Molina in Ruiseñada. Nearby is the Cueva de la Meaza, a listed cave with a single wavy red painted sign, which is not open to visits.
facts: Cueva de la Meaza (Bien de Interés Cultural, not visitable)

name: Ermita de Santa Ana (Pirgo)
summary: Neo-Gothic chapel in Pirgo, in Ruiseñada parish on the slopes of Monte Corona.

name: Casa de Juntas de Puente San Miguel
summary: The meeting house where the Province of Cantabria was founded in 1778, remembered every 28 July with the Festival of the Cantabrian Institutions at the nearby Ermita de los Valles.
facts: Fiesta de las Instituciones de Cantabria, 28 July

name: Casa natal de José María de Pereda (Polanco)
summary: Birthplace of the novelist José María de Pereda in Polanco, named in the leaflet as a key place in Cantabrian identity.
uncertain: Leaflet only mentions it; no visiting details.

name: Abadía de Santa María de Viaceli (Cóbreces)
summary: Trappist abbey in Cóbreces where the monks make a well-known cheese; Cóbreces also holds a cheese fair on the first weekend of July.
facts: Feria del Queso, first weekend of July (Cóbreces)

name: Ría de Mogro (Abra del Pas)
summary: The estuary where the river Pas meets the sea, the eastern starting point of the Costa Central.

name: Playa de Usgo
summary: Wild, secluded beach on the Miengo coast, on the Costa Quebrada coastal path between Robayera and Cuchía.

name: Costa Quebrada path: Robayera to Cuchía
summary: Coastal walk of about 7 km one way from Robayera beach via Punta del Águila, Usgo beach, Punta del Cuerno and Los Caballos beach to Cuchía. More routes on the Miengo council website.
uncertain: Same route as "Ruta Costa Quebrada (Robayera – Cuchía)" in cantur-routes.en.json; not added to Notion here to avoid a duplicate row.

name: Playa de la Ribera (Suances)
summary: Small urban beach on the Ría de San Martín next to the fishing and sports port, with calm water, ideal for young children. Gentle slope into the water.
facts: Red Cross, with boat; danger zone marked by buoys
Promenade, parking nearby, bins, showers, first-aid post, seasonal kiosks
On foot and by wheeled access

name: Playa de la Riberuca (Suances)
summary: Quiet estuary beach inside La Ribera landscape park, linked to the foot and cycle path, good for a gentle walk. Calm water with an anchorage; easy, gentle access.
facts: Parking, bins, showers, first-aid post, picnic area

name: Playa de la Tablía (Suances)
summary: Perhaps Suances's most unspoilt beach, open to the sea with big cliffs and strong waves, popular with surfers. Not lifeguarded; reached by a steep path down the cliff. Small car park nearby and a clifftop viewpoint; the Suances-Tagle cycle lane passes by.
uncertain: The 'Mirador Playa de la Tablía' is already on the map; this is the beach below it.

name: Centro de Buceo Calypso (Playa de Usil, Mogro)
summary: Dive centre on Usil beach offering boat and shore dives, snorkelling, try-dives (pool or sea), courses and boat trips. Dive sites include the five Islas Conejeras (a protected bird reserve), Faro de Suances, Roca Blanca and Punta Ballota, where the wreck of the mail ship Isla de Cuba lies. Estuary trips pass osprey nesting platforms.
facts: Paseo Marítimo 192, Playa de Usil, Mogro

name: Palacio y Capilla-Panteón de Sobrellano
summary: Official leaflet for the Sobrellano estate: guided visits to the palace or the chapel-pantheon should be bought or booked well ahead; on the day, tickets are sold only at the ticket office subject to space. The gardens are not guided and have no capacity limit. Info panels mark 8 points around the estate.
facts: Free-roaming, not guided, no capacity limit

name: Museo de Altamira – guided Neocueva + museum visit
summary: Guided visit to the Neocueva and the Altamira museum, entry included, for all ages, at 15:30 every day except Sundays, holidays and Mondays. Booking essential. Ticket desk at the museum.
facts: 15.00 euros; free for children up to 8
Daily except Sundays, public holidays and Mondays
Av. Sanz de Sautuola s/n, Santillana
Birch and hazel grove near the Neocueva recreating the Ice Age vegetation

name: Casas del Águila y la Parra – visit details
summary: Temporary exhibitions in two 16th-17th-century houses on the Plaza Mayor next to the town hall. Closed on Mondays; visits are free.
matchesExistingPlace: Casas del Águila y la Parra

name: Zoo de Santillana – details
summary: 60,000 m2 zoo with primates, big cats, a tropical butterfly house and waterfowl, a botanical collection of 300+ trees, a Quaternary Park recreating Altamira-era species, and a farm where children can touch domestic animals.

name: Museo Jesús Otero – visit details
summary: Municipal cultural centre opened in 1994 beside the Colegiata, with the María Sanz de Sautuola library, archive and exhibition rooms. Free visit includes the garden with six large sculptures, two rooms and a covered patio.

name: Museo Diocesano Regina Coeli – collection
summary: Opened in 1967 in the Regina Coeli convent, with over 800 works from Cantabrian parishes (popular and Gothic sculpture, silks, ivories, enamels, silverwork) and a nationally known book-restoration workshop.

name: Colegiata de Santa Juliana – contact
summary: Romanesque collegiate church with cloister; listed Bien de Interés Cultural in 1889. Separate cloister entrance marked on the town map.

name: Palacio de Peredo-Barreda – garden and museum
summary: Exhibition centre (Caja Cantabria) since 2000 with original furniture, art and a notable library. Its walled garden holds a 25 m ginkgo and a horse chestnut nearly 4 m round.
facts: Museo de Caja Cantabria, C/ Santo Domingo 8

name: Museo de la Tortura – alternative name
summary: Listed in the official town map as the 'Museo de la Inquisición El Solar' and in the guide directory as Museo de la Tortura, C/ Bertrand Clisson 1.

guide: Santillana Del Mar, un lugar para admirar
name: Museo del Barquillero (Casa de los Abades)
summary: The illustrated monuments map marks the Casa de la Archiduquesa / de los Abades as an exhibition space housing the 'Museo del Barquillero'.
uncertain: Map label only; no hours or prices.

name: Antiguo Seminario Mayor – Fundación Comillas
summary: The restored former Pontifical University on La Cardosa hill now houses the CIESE-Comillas university centre (Spanish language and Hispanic studies); its noble rooms are open to visitors. The 1892 entrance gate by Domènech has pages holding the papal arms.

name: El Capricho de Gaudí – phone
summary: Listed in the Comillas guide's useful numbers; stands inside the Sobrellano park next to the palace and chapel.

name: Puerto de Comillas – history
summary: Paid for by the townspeople and finished in 1716; the last Cantabrian port to keep whaling. Three sentry boxes, a small fort and cannons survive; a timber floodgate can close the inner basin in storms.

name: Playa de la Concha (Suances) – beach facts
summary: Suances's busiest, most accessible beach with all services, host of summer volleyball, handball, football and rugby tournaments.
facts: 1.5 km promenade from La Ribera, parking nearby, first aid, drinking water, showers, surfboard hire, picnic area

name: Playa de los Locos – beach facts
summary: Declared a Natural Surf Reserve; one of Spain's best-known surf spots. Open beach with strong waves.
facts: Parking nearby, first aid, drinking water, showers, picnic area

name: Playa El Sable (Tagle) – beach facts
summary: Small sandy beach between cliffs, rustic and quiet; walkers can follow the cliffs to Punta Ballota. Confirms that 'Tagle' and 'El Sable' are the same beach.
facts: Parking, first aid, drinking water, showers, picnic area
uncertain: This place is held back (data/held-back.json), not on the map.

name: Playa de Santa Justa (Ubiarco) – facilities
summary: Small cove beach with restored surroundings, a children's playground, a hotel and picnic benches; paths along the cliffs lead to the San Telmo wall. The chapel was listed as local heritage in 2010.
